topic.angle: A maths professor spots a chip error

card.title: The chip that got division wrong

body.claim: In June 1994, Thomas Nicely, a professor of mathematics at Lynchburg College, noticed inconsistencies in his calculations. The cause was Intel's Pentium processor, which returned incorrect results when dividing certain pairs of high-precision numbers.
body.why: Missing values in a lookup table used by the floating-point division algorithm led to small errors. In December 1994, Intel recalled the defective processors, and in January 1995 it announced a pre-tax charge of $475 million.
